title: Brown Sugar and Cinnamon Stovetop Oatmeal for the Week
description: A big pot of creamy rolled oats cooked in milk and water, sweetened lightly with brown sugar and studded with raisins. Six bowls for under 50 cents each, and it reheats well all week.
notes: Old-fashioned rolled oats give a creamy pot with some texture; quick oats turn to paste and steel-cut oats need twice the liquid and time. Use certified gluten-free rolled oats if anyone at the table avoids gluten, since standard oats are often processed alongside wheat. Swap the milk for water or an unsweetened nut-free plant milk and leave out the butter to make it dairy-free. Cool the pot, portion into containers, and refrigerate within 2 hours; it keeps 5 days. Reheat a portion in a small pot or the microwave with a splash of milk or water, stirring, until steaming hot (165°F). The oats thicken as they chill, so expect to add 2 to 4 tablespoons of liquid per bowl. Top with sliced banana, a spoonful of peanut butter, or toasted seeds for a bigger breakfast.
instructions: Combine the water, milk, and salt in a large saucepan or 3-quart pot and bring to a gentle boil over medium-high heat, watching so the milk does not foam over.

Stir in the oats, lower the heat to medium-low, and simmer uncovered for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring every minute or two and scraping the bottom, until the oats are tender and the liquid has turned creamy.
Add the brown sugar, cinnamon, and raisins and cook 2 minutes more, until the raisins plump and the oatmeal mounds softly on the spoon. It will thicken further as it sits.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the butter and vanilla, if using. Let it stand 3 minutes before serving; the oats finish setting as they rest.
Serve hot with a splash of cold milk, or cool and portion into six containers for the week, reheating each bowl with a few tablespoons of milk or water.

title: Freezer Breakfast Burritos with Potatoes, Eggs, and Black Beans
description: Crisp skillet potatoes, soft scrambled eggs, black beans, and cheddar rolled into flour tortillas and frozen for the week. Eight burritos for about $1 each, and each one reheats in the microwave in 3 minutes.
notes: Let every filling cool to room temperature before rolling, since warm filling steams the tortilla and makes it tear and ice over in the freezer. Keep the salsa to a spoonful per burrito for the same reason, and serve extra on the side. Pinto beans or leftover refried beans work in place of the black beans, and 4 oz of browned breakfast sausage or chopped thick-cut bacon can go in for a meatier version. Monterey Jack melts a little more smoothly than cheddar. Wrapped burritos keep refrigerated for 4 days or frozen for 3 months. To reheat from frozen, remove the foil, wrap in a damp paper towel, and microwave for 2 to 3 minutes, flipping halfway, until the center reaches 165°F; or bake foil-wrapped at 375°F for 30 to 35 minutes. Refrigerate any cooked filling within 2 hours.

ingredients.name: russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
black beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
tomato salsa or pico de gallo, drained of excess liquid

instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the potatoes in an even layer, sprinkle with 3/4 teaspoon of the salt, and cook undisturbed for 5 minutes, until the bottoms are browned.

Stir the potatoes, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for 10 to 12 minutes more, turning every few minutes, until they are crisp outside and a cube mashes easily with a fork. Stir in the chili powder, cumin, and black beans and cook for 2 minutes to warm the beans through, then spread the mixture on a plate to cool.

Whisk the eggs, milk, the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, and the pepper in a medium bowl until no streaks remain. Wipe out the skillet, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon oil over medium-low heat, and pour in the eggs.

Cook the eggs, pushing them slowly from the edges to the center with a spatula, for 3 to 4 minutes, until they form soft, glossy curds that are just barely set; they will cook more during reheating. Scrape onto a second plate and let both fillings cool for 15 to 20 minutes.

Warm the tortillas in the dry skillet or the microwave for 20 seconds so they fold without cracking. Lay one flat and put a scant 1/2 cup of the potato and bean mixture across the lower third, then an eighth of the eggs, 3 tablespoons of cheese, 1 tablespoon of salsa, and a few scallions if using.
Fold the bottom edge up over the filling, fold in both sides, and roll tightly away from you into a snug log. Set seam side down and repeat with the remaining tortillas and fillings.

To eat now, brown the burritos seam side down in the dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes per side, until crisp and golden. To store, wrap each one tightly in foil or parchment, slide them into a labeled freezer bag, and refrigerate or freeze.

title: Yogurt Bowls with Skillet Cinnamon Apples and Toasted Oats
description: Plain whole-milk yogurt topped with apples softened in butter and brown sugar, and a handful of oats toasted in the same pan. Takes 15 minutes, costs about 75 cents a bowl, and the toppings keep for days.
notes: Any firm apple works; cheaper varieties like Gala or Fuji hold their shape, and there is no need to peel them. Greek yogurt makes a thicker bowl, while plain whole-milk yogurt is both cheaper and creamier at breakfast. For a dairy-free bowl use an unsweetened plant-based yogurt and swap the butter for coconut oil, which removes the milk allergen. Use certified gluten-free rolled oats if needed. The apples keep refrigerated for 4 days and the toasted oats keep in a jar at room temperature for a week, so make a double batch of both for fast mornings. Refrigerate the cooked apples within 2 hours; serve them cold or warmed for 30 seconds in the microwave.

ingredients.name: medium apples (about 1 1/4 lb), cored and cut into 1/2-inch pieces

instructions: Melt 1 tablespoon of the butter in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the apples, brown sugar, cinnamon, and 1/8 teaspoon of the salt and stir to coat.

Cook, stirring every minute or so, for 6 to 8 minutes, until the apples are tender when pierced but still hold their shape and the juices have thickened into a light syrup. Stir in the lemon juice and scrape the apples into a medium bowl.

Wipe the skillet, return it to medium heat, and melt the remaining 1 tablespoon butter. Add the oats and the remaining 1/8 teaspoon salt and toast, stirring constantly, for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden and nutty-smelling. Tip onto a plate to cool so they stay crisp.
Divide the yogurt among four bowls. Spoon the warm or cold apples and their syrup over the top, scatter on the toasted oats, and finish with a drizzle of honey if you like.

title: No-Knead Sandwich Bread for the Week
description: A soft, close-crumbed loaf from a wet dough you stir together in five minutes, let rise, and bake in a loaf pan. About $1 in ingredients, and the only work is waiting. Makes 14 slices for toast and sandwiches.
notes: Weighing the flour matters more than usual here because the dough is wet on purpose; if you must use cups, spoon the flour in and level it. Bread flour gives a taller loaf, but all-purpose flour works with a slightly softer crumb. Active dry yeast can be used in the same amount; stir it into the warm water first and wait 5 minutes until it foams. Swap the butter for 2 tablespoons of neutral oil to make the loaf dairy-free. The dough can rise overnight in the refrigerator after the first mix; let it sit at room temperature for 30 minutes before shaping. Cool completely before slicing or the crumb will be gummy. Store sliced in a bag at room temperature for 3 days, or freeze slices with parchment between them for 3 months and toast from frozen.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan

instructions: Whisk the flour, yeast, salt, and sugar together in a large bowl. Pour in the warm water and the melted butter and stir with a sturdy spoon for about 1 minute, until no dry flour remains; the dough will be shaggy and sticky, closer to a thick batter than a kneadable dough.
Cover the bowl with a plate or plastic wrap and let it rise at warm room temperature for 2 to 3 hours, until doubled and bubbly on top. In a cool kitchen it can take 4 hours.

Butter a 9 by 5-inch loaf pan generously. Wet a spatula, scrape the dough away from the sides of the bowl, and tip it into the pan. Wet your fingers and nudge it into an even layer that reaches the corners.

Cover loosely and let it rise again for 45 to 60 minutes, until the dough has domed about 1 inch above the rim of the pan. About 20 minutes before it is ready, heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the top is deep golden and an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 200°F. If the top browns before then, tent it with foil for the last 10 minutes.

Let the loaf sit in the pan for 5 minutes, then run a knife around the edge and turn it out onto a wire rack. Brush the top with a little melted butter if you like a soft crust, and cool completely, at least 1 hour, before slicing into 14 slices.

title: Indian-Style Cabbage with Cumin Seeds and Turmeric
description: Thinly sliced cabbage cooked until just tender with cumin seeds, ginger, and turmeric, finished with lime and cilantro. One $2 head of cabbage becomes six generous servings of the side that makes dal and rice a full dinner.
equipment: 12-inch skillet or wide pot with lid
notes: This style of dry cabbage dish is often called patta gobi sabzi; the cabbage should be tender with a little bite, not soft and sweet like a braise. A heavy pan and a lid are what keep it from drying out before it cooks through. Leave the chile out for children and add a squeeze more lime instead. Frozen peas make it a little more substantial for almost no extra cost. A pinch of garam masala stirred in at the end adds warmth. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 4 days; reheat in a skillet with a spoonful of water until steaming (165°F), or eat it cold folded into a wrap.

ingredients.name: serrano or green chile, thinly sliced
small head green cabbage (about 2 lb), cored and sliced 1/4 inch thick

instructions: Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet or wide pot over medium-high heat until it shimmers, about 1 minute. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 20 to 30 seconds, until they darken a shade and smell toasty.
Add the ginger and chile, if using, and stir for 30 seconds. Add the turmeric and coriander and stir for 10 seconds more, just until fragrant; do not let the spices scorch.
Add the cabbage in two or three handfuls, stirring after each so it wilts enough to make room. Sprinkle with the salt and toss to coat everything in the spiced oil.

Cover, lower the heat to medium, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the cabbage is tender with a little bite and the bottom is beginning to brown in spots. Add the frozen peas for the last 3 minutes if using.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium-high, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes to drive off any liquid in the pan. Take it off the heat, stir in the lime juice and cilantro, taste for salt, and serve.

title: Moroccan-Style Carrot Salad with Cumin and Lemon
description: Carrots simmered until just tender, then dressed warm with garlic, cumin, paprika, lemon, and olive oil so they soak up the flavor as they cool. Serve cold or at room temperature; about 35 cents a serving and better on day two.
notes: Cut the carrots evenly so they cook at the same rate; thick ends can be halved lengthwise first. Dressing them while warm is the point, since cold carrots will not absorb the oil and spices. Cilantro can replace the parsley, and a pinch of ground cinnamon is traditional in some versions. The salad keeps refrigerated for 4 days and improves overnight, which makes it a good lunchbox side. Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking. Let it sit at room temperature for 15 minutes before serving so the olive oil loosens.

ingredients.name: carrots, peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick on the diagonal
kosher salt, plus more for the cooking water

instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil with a generous spoonful of salt. Add the carrots and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until a knife slides in easily but the slices still hold a firm edge. Drain well in a colander.

While the carrots cook, warm the olive oil in a small skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic, cumin, paprika, and cayenne, if using, and stir for about 45 seconds, until fragrant and the garlic is just softened, not browned.
Scrape the spiced oil into a medium bowl and whisk in the lemon juice and the 3/4 teaspoon salt. Add the hot drained carrots and toss to coat.
Let the carrots cool in the dressing for at least 20 minutes, tossing once or twice. Stir in the parsley, taste for salt and lemon, and serve at room temperature or chilled.

title: Refried Pinto Beans from One Pound of Dried Beans
description: Simmer a pound of dried pintos with onion and garlic until creamy, then mash them in the same pot with their own broth, cumin, and fried onion. Eight servings for under 30 cents each, and they freeze well.
notes: Fresh dried beans cook in about 1 1/2 hours; beans that have sat in the pantry a year or more can take 2 1/2 hours, so start checking early and keep simmering until they are fully creamy inside. No soaking is needed, but an 8-hour soak shortens the cooking time by about 30 minutes. Lard is the traditional fat and gives a richer flavor if you have it. The bean broth is seasoning, not waste: thin the refried beans with it and save any extra for soup, or hold back a few cups of whole beans in broth for another meal. Melted sharp cheddar on top adds the milk allergen. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours; the beans keep 5 days and freeze for 3 months. Reheat with a splash of water, stirring, until steaming hot (165°F).

ingredients.name: dried pinto beans (450 g), picked over and rinsed
large yellow onion, half left whole and half finely diced

instructions: Put the beans, water, the whole onion half, the 2 whole garlic cloves, and the bay leaf in a large pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower the heat so the surface barely bubbles, cover partially, and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, stirring occasionally and adding hot water if the beans are not covered.

Stir in 1 1/2 teaspoons of the salt when the beans are soft enough to crush against the side of the pot, then simmer for 15 minutes more, until they are creamy all the way through with no chalky center. Discard the onion half, garlic cloves, and bay leaf.
Set a colander over a large bowl and drain the beans, saving all of the broth. Wipe out the pot, add the oil, and heat over medium heat for 1 minute.
Cook the diced onion and jalapeño, if using, for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and golden at the edges. Add the minced garlic and cumin and stir for 30 seconds.
Return the beans to the pot with 2 cups of the broth and bring to a simmer. Mash with a potato masher, working around the pot, until mostly smooth with some whole beans left.

Cook for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until the beans thicken to the consistency of soft mashed potatoes, adding more broth if they get stiff. Season with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste, and serve; they thicken further as they cool.

title: Southern-Style Collard Greens with Smoked Paprika and Vinegar
description: Collards simmered with onion, garlic, broth, and a little smoked paprika until silky, finished with cider vinegar. Two bunches of greens feed six for about 60 cents a serving, with or without bacon.
equipment: large pot or Dutch oven with lid
notes: Wash the leaves in two changes of water, since collards hold grit in their folds. For a traditional version, cook 3 slices of chopped thick-cut bacon in the pot first and use the fat in place of most of the oil; that removes the vegan and vegetarian tags but adds no new allergens. Simmering is the key, and the greens are not done until a thick piece is fully tender, so taste one before you stop. Lacinato or curly kale cooks in about half the time. Leftovers keep refrigerated for 4 days and taste better the next day; refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat until steaming (165°F). The liquid at the bottom of the pot is worth saving for beans or cornbread.

ingredients.name: collard greens (about 2 lb), tough center ribs removed and leaves cut into 1-inch ribbons
apple cider vinegar, plus more for serving
Louisiana-style cayenne pepper hot sauce, for serving

instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika, and red pepper flakes and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the collards in big handfuls, stirring and letting each batch wilt for a minute before adding the next; the pot will be very full at first and settle quickly.

Pour in the broth, add the vinegar, sugar, the remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt, and the black pepper, and bring to a boil. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 35 to 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, until the leaves are silky and no longer chewy.
Uncover and simmer for 5 minutes to reduce the liquid slightly. Taste and add more salt or vinegar as needed, and serve with hot sauce at the table.

title: Chewy Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
description: Soft-centered, crisp-edged oatmeal cookies with plenty of raisins and a little cinnamon, from one bowl and pantry staples. Two dozen for about $3, or roughly 15 cents a cookie.
notes: The butter should be soft enough to dent with a finger but not greasy; if it melts, the cookies spread thin. Chilling the scooped dough for 30 minutes gives thicker cookies with a chewier center. Dried cranberries can stand in for the raisins, and 1/2 cup of chopped walnuts adds crunch but adds the tree nut allergen. Semisweet chocolate chips instead of raisins are a reliable swap at the same amount. Store cooled cookies in an airtight container at room temperature for 4 days. Scooped raw dough freezes for 3 months; bake from frozen, adding 2 minutes.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds, and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
Beat the butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar in a large bowl with a wooden spoon or hand mixer for about 2 minutes, until lighter in color and fluffy. Beat in the egg and vanilla until smooth.

Stir the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt together in a separate bowl, then add to the butter mixture and stir just until no dry streaks remain. Stir in the oats and raisins; the dough will be thick.
Scoop the dough in 2-tablespoon mounds (about 40 g each) onto the sheets, 12 per sheet and 2 inches apart, and press each one down slightly.
Bake for 11 to 13 minutes, switching the sheets between racks halfway, until the edges are golden brown and the centers look set but still soft. They will firm up as they cool.
Let the cookies rest on the sheets for 5 minutes, then move them to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Cinnamon Apple Crumble with Oat Topping
description: Apples baked under a buttery oat and brown sugar topping until bubbling at the edges. Cheap apples are all it needs, so a whole pan costs about $5, or around 55 cents a square, and it is good warm, cold, or for breakfast with yogurt.
notes: Mixing two kinds of apples, one that holds its shape and one that softens, gives the best filling, but a single bag of whatever is on sale works well. Keep the butter cold so the topping bakes into crumbs rather than melting into a sheet; if your kitchen is warm, chill the topping while you cut the apples. For a dairy-free version use cold coconut oil in place of the butter, which removes the milk allergen. The baked crumble keeps covered at room temperature for 1 day or refrigerated for 4 days; refrigerate within 2 hours if you pack it into lunchboxes. Reheat squares at 350°F for 10 minutes to crisp the top again. Unbaked, it can be assembled and refrigerated for a day, then baked straight from the fridge with 5 extra minutes.

ingredients.name: medium apples (about 2 1/2 lb), peeled, cored, and sliced 1/4 inch thick
cold unsalted butter (113 g), cut into 1/2-inch cubes

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center and butter a 9-inch square baking dish.
Toss the apples in a large bowl with the granulated sugar, cornstarch, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, lemon juice, and 1/8 teaspoon salt until evenly coated. Spread them in the dish and press down lightly.

Stir the flour, oats, brown sugar, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1/4 teaspoon salt together in a medium bowl. Add the cold butter and cut it in with a pastry cutter or your fingertips until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs with some pea-size pieces of butter remaining.
Squeeze handfuls of the topping together and crumble them over the apples in an even layer, leaving some larger clumps.

Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until the topping is deep golden, the apples are tender when pierced through the top with a knife, and the juices bubble thickly at the edges. If the top browns early, tent loosely with foil.
Cool in the dish for at least 20 minutes so the juices set before cutting into nine squares. Serve warm or at room temperature, with yogurt or a spoonful of vanilla ice cream if you like.
